title: The Concept of Social Roles and Scripts
text:
Sociology examines social roles as sets of expected behaviors attached to particular status positions within a group or society. These roles provide structural guidance, dictating appropriate actions for individuals based on their perceived position (e.g., parent, student, employee). The performance of these scripts helps maintain predictable social order and predictability.

However, adherence is not absolute; the tension between ascribed roles and achieved roles often creates situational conflict. When expectations are unclear or contradictory, the individual experiences role strain, which can destabilize both personal identity and group function. Analyzing this dynamic reveals how deeply ingrained norms underpin collective action.
